official.deadline_note: GRIPS publishes no central YLP deadline. Its 'Application Deadlines by Program, 2027-2028' table lists YLP under 'Apply through a sponsoring organization' with Contact Organization 'Japanese Embassy' and Application Deadline 'Varies'; the Scholarships Eligibility and Details chart states 'deadlines differ by a sponsoring organization'. GRIPS's Japanese YLP page publishes, as last year's results, an application acceptance period (願書受付時期) of July to October and notification of results (合格発表時期) the following April. The operative date is set by the recommending authority in the applicant's own country.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 cycle (YLP Brochure 2027-2028; GRIPS 'We are accepting applications for admission to GRIPS for 2027-2028')
official.status_note: GRIPS has published the 2027-2028 YLP Brochure, the 2027-2028 application guide and forms, and the Scholarship Eligibility and Details chart dated August 2026; the Scholarships / Tuition and Fees page lists the Young Leaders Program (YLP) with the 'Japanese Government - YLP-MEXT Scholarship' as available for international students, and GRIPS states it is accepting applications for 2027-2028 admission. GRIPS's How to Apply page lists YLP among the programmes for which 'Application ... should be made through the sponsoring organization', so the round is open at nominating-authority level rather than to direct GRIPS applicants.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'Application fee, admission fee and tuition are waivered' (YLP 2027-2028 brochure, Scholarships section). The GRIPS Scholarship Eligibility and Details chart lists 'Application fee, admission fee, and tuition' in YLP Scholarship Coverage. For reference, GRIPS publishes its own charges for self-financed applicants as application fee 30,000 yen, admission fee 282,000 yen and tuition 642,960 yen yearly, 'subject to change'.
benefits: An allowance of 242,000 yen per month (in FY 2026; amount is subject to change) will be provided to grantees during the term of the scholarship
Application fee, admission fee and tuition are waivered

An economy-class air ticket from your home country to Japan upon enrollment at GRIPS and an economy-class air ticket from Japan to your home country upon completion of your studies at GRIPS will be provided

eligibility: Young public administrators and government officials who are expected to play active roles in the future as national leaders in their home countries, with a minimum of three years of full-time work experience (five is preferable) in the field in the applicant's home country

Applicants are not eligible if they are unable to travel to Japan by the last date of the period specified by GRIPS; people who are active members of military forces or civilians employed by the military during any part of the scholarship period, who are enrolled in a Japanese university under Student status, or who plan to enroll at a Japanese university as a privately financed international student between the time of application and the time the scholarship period is due to commence, are also ineligible

official.application_route: Apply through the recommending authority / Japanese embassy listed for your country on the GRIPS page - YLP has no direct GRIPS application route.
official.citizenship_residency: Restricted to designated countries. School of Government accepts students from 29 countries: China, Republic of Korea, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Viet Nam, Laos, Cambodia, Mongolia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Bangladesh, India, Bhutan, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Australia, Hungary, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania, Republic of Türkiye. School of Local Governance accepts students from 20 countries: China, Republic of Korea, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, Viet Nam, Laos, Cambodia, Mongolia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, India, Bhutan, Pakistan, Republic of Türkiye, Hungary, Czech Republic, Poland, Romania. GRIPS's Scholarship Eligibility and Details chart additionally lists the 2027-2028 eligible countries per school (28 for School of Government; 17 for School of Local Governance) and states eligible countries are subject to change.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. GRIPS states the scholarship listed for YLP is for international students only, funded by the Japanese Government (MEXT). GRIPS also accepts Japanese students through the separate YLP Japan admissions route.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Public administration and government service. The programme is open to exceptionally promising young government officials with considerable working experience in the area of public administration; applicants must be serving public administrators or government officials, and loss of that status before completion makes them ineligible. The School of Government focuses on national policy-making; the School of Local Governance focuses on enhancement of local governance in education, health, social welfare and local development.
official.research_requirement: The programme requires a final policy paper based on Independent Study (all students present their research in June or July); GRIPS states this programme does not use the separate Research Proposal form, which is required only for two-year master's and Ph.D. programmes.
official.duration: 1 year (October enrolment, September graduation), leading to a Master of Public Policy
official.description: The Young Leaders Program (YLP) at GRIPS is a special one-year master's degree program in Public Policy, taught entirely in English, for exceptionally promising young government officials. It was introduced by the Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology in 2001 to foster future national leaders in designated countries, build comprehensive human networks among the leaders of nations, establish friendly relationships among the countries involved, and improve the quality of policymaking in the participating countries. It is fully supported, including full scholarships for all students, by the Japanese government.
official.program_type: Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarship programme hosted at GRIPS; Master's degree programme (Master of Public Policy)
official.english_requirement: Proficient in English with a TOEFL iBT score of 79/120, IELTS Academic score of 6.0 or equivalent (4.5/6 is also stated)

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-year Master of Public Policy at GRIPS in Tokyo taught entirely in English, running October enrolment to September graduation, and every admitted YLP student receives the MEXT scholarship - you are not competing against a separate funding pool or mixing scholarship types. The money is set by the Japanese government rather than negotiated per applicant: JPY 242,000 a month (FY 2026 figure), waivered application, admission and tuition fees, economy-class round-trip airfare and required field trip costs, plus Tokyo International Exchange Center housing. The catch is not academic merit but the route: there is no direct GRIPS application, so your real deadline is whatever your own ministry or embassy sets, and GRIPS only publishes 'Varies' with the Japanese Embassy as contact. Your genuine out-of-pocket exposure is Tokyo living costs beyond the stipend, visa and medical costs, and moving-in expenses; if you cannot secure a full year's release from your post, this is not the right programme.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Serving civil servants from one of the 29 School of Government or 20 School of Local Governance countries who already have three to five years of public-administration work and can secure a nomination from the authority GRIPS lists for their country.
application_readiness_checklist: Find your country on GRIPS's List of Recommending Authorities and check both the School of Government and School of Local Governance columns - the two schools are sometimes nominated by different bodies, and a country on one list may be absent from the other.

Request the application form from your Japanese embassy or recommending authority rather than from GRIPS - the brochure states applicants obtain the form there, and GRIPS publishes no YLP application pack of its own - and treat that authority's own recommendation letter as a separate document you must also request.

Book TOEFL iBT (aim for 79+) or IELTS Academic 6.0 early enough that the official report arrives inside the July-October window GRIPS publishes; this is a published eligibility threshold, not a preference.
Order certified English-language transcripts, degree certificates and a certificate of health now, since the whole file goes in hard copy and medical appointments are slow to schedule.

Confirm with your HR or personnel directorate that your organisation will release you for a full year away and will re-employ you afterwards - GRIPS expects graduates to return to their former governmental organisations.
Verify you have not applied to any other GRIPS programme (including MEP) in the same academic year, which would void the application.
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to GRIPS: GRIPS explicitly lists YLP under applications that 'should be made through the sponsoring organization', and only accepts the nominating body's submission as an application.
Applying to more than one GRIPS programme in one academic year - the FAQ rules this out in any circumstances, including external applications such as YLP and MEP.
Missing the three-year full-time public-administration experience requirement, or being 40 or over as of 1 October 2027.
Submitting a recycled file: GRIPS states no supporting document submitted in a previous year can be reused for a later application.

Falling into one of the brochure's hard ineligibility grounds: being unable to travel to Japan by the last date of the period GRIPS specifies; being an active military member or a civilian employed by the military at any point in the scholarship period; or already being enrolled, or planning to enrol, at a Japanese university under Student status.
Assuming the YLP brochure is optional: it is the only published source of the eligibility thresholds, the English score and the document list.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Covered: monthly stipend of JPY 242,000, application/admission fees and tuition, economy-class round-trip airfare and required field trip costs; housing is offered at the MEXT-built Tokyo International Exchange Center residence halls run by JASSO. Still on you: Tokyo living costs above the stipend, visa application and residence-card costs, the medical examination, and initial relocation, moving-in and furnishing costs. For scale, GRIPS's self-financed charges are 30,000 yen application, 282,000 yen admission and 642,960 yen yearly tuition, so the waiver is a large share of the award's value. Accommodation is offered rather than free, and family rooms cost more than singles.
document_audit: Three separate letters are involved: the recommending authority's recommendation letter plus two letters from an immediate superior at work or your supervising professor - applicants routinely supply only two and then cannot complete the file.
'Official evidence of English ability' means the official score document, not a printout of a self-service online result; request the score report from ETS or IELTS directly.
Official transcripts of academic record and graduation/degree certificates are required, so local-language documents need certified English translations - build this in before the window opens.
The file goes in hard copy, so courier time to the recommending authority counts against the deadline; there is no online submission portal for YLP.
A certificate of health is on the mandatory list and visa processing depends on it, so book the medical examination before the window opens rather than after nomination.
Essays are required but no length, prompt or template is published, and GRIPS publishes no YLP-specific form - ask the recommending authority what it expects rather than guessing.
alerts: GRIPS publishes no YLP deadline at all: its 2027-2028 deadline table lists YLP with 'Japanese Embassy' as contact organization and 'Varies' as the deadline, so do not diarise the November 20, 2026 / November 27, 2026 dates shown elsewhere on that page - those are for MEXT University Recommendation and other GRIPS-administered programmes.
The JPY 242,000 stipend is the FY 2026 figure and GRIPS notes the amount is subject to change, so treat it as indicative for the 2027 intake.
You must keep your status as a public administrator or government official: losing it before completion makes you ineligible, which constrains any career move during the year.
Grantees who are absent from the university for long periods stop receiving the scholarship, so plan the year as continuous residence in Tokyo.

The School of Government and School of Local Governance have different country lists and, in many countries, different recommending authorities - confirm both before choosing which to apply for, and re-check the current GRIPS chart rather than the brochure, because GRIPS notes eligible countries are subject to change without notice.
GRIPS also admits Japanese students to YLP through a separate Japanese-language route, so the international quota is not the entire cohort.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Request the form from your Japanese embassy or recommending authority, build the hard-copy file including the authority's own recommendation letter, and submit to that authority by its deadline - GRIPS treats that submission as your application to GRIPS, then runs admission screening and passes successful candidates into the MEXT/YLP scholarship route.
